name: Gao PAE versus TURP
question: How do prostatic arterial embolization and TURP compare for symptoms, urinary function, and complications in men with BPH?

design.population: 114 consenting men with benign prostatic hyperplasia were randomized to PAE or TURP.

verdictNote: Both improved outcomes; TURP improved several early measures more, while PAE had more reported complications.
takeaway: In 114 men randomized to prostatic arterial embolization or TURP, both procedures improved measured BPH outcomes through 24 months. TURP improved symptoms and flow more at one and three months; PAE had more overall adverse events and complications.

reports.label: Primary randomized report
reports.citation: Gao YA, Huang Y, Zhang R, et al. "Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Prostatic Arterial Embolization versus Transurethral Resection of the Prostate—A Prospective, Randomized, and Controlled Clinical Trial." *Radiology.* 2014;270(3):920-928. doi:10.1148/radiol.13122803
reports.followUp: Outcomes assessed at 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months; follow-up completion not stated in abstract

results.endpoint: IPSS, quality of life, peak flow, and postvoid residual
results.measure: Between-group comparative improvement at 1 and 3 months
results.note: All six measured functional outcomes improved from baseline in both arms at every visit (P=0.001); the abstract does not identify a prespecified primary endpoint or provide absolute changes.
